page.title: Target
page.purpose: Explain one target completely: what was probed on which node, what it proved, which device-control strategy would drive it, and precisely what is missing when it is unavailable.

priorities.statement: A terminal target explains why it is terminal, and offers nothing to click.
priorities.notes: 'No Apple toolchain exists for Linux' is a complete answer. Suggesting a remedy would be false.

priorities.statement: Every probed capability is listed with its result and the time it was probed.
priorities.notes: Xcode version, simulator runtimes, GUI session, and signing identity each fail differently and each needs its own line.

priorities.statement: The driving strategy and its capability tier are named before a run, not only after.
priorities.notes: An operator should know they are about to get pixel-grade evidence before spending a run on it.

states.description: A fully available simulator target on a macOS node.
A native iOS target on the Linux host. Permanently unsupported, explained, with no remediation affordance.
The macOS node is online but has no logged-in GUI session, so the simulator cannot run. Distinct from a missing Xcode.
Xcode is present but the x86_64 universal simulator runtime variant is not installed on this Intel host.
A physical iPhone reachable through device-control. The xcuitest strategy is unavailable pending enrollment; the mirror strategy is available but pixel-grade.

claims.statement: A target in the unsupported state presents an explanation and no action control.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-003. An affordance implies a path; there is none, and offering one wastes the operator's time on something structurally impossible.

claims.statement: Missing Xcode, missing runtime variant, missing GUI session, and missing signing identity produce four different messages with four different next actions.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-003. These fail for unrelated reasons and a single generic 'macOS node not ready' would make all four undiagnosable.

claims.statement: A physical-device target names which strategy would drive it and whether that strategy is semantic or pixel-grade, before a run is started.
claims.rationale: S2I-P1-002. Pixel-grade evidence is non-promotable; an operator must know that before spending a run rather than discovering it in review.

claims.statement: Every capability result displays when it was probed.
claims.rationale: Capability is a measurement, and a measurement without a timestamp cannot be judged current.
